springs.name: vawe snappy
springs.note: indicator() gives this spring to the edge of a moving indicator that leads the move.

springs.name: vawe default
springs.note: It is the default of spring(), track() and springLinear(), and the trailing edge in indicator(). The numbers equal react-spring default.

springs.name: vawe heavy
springs.note: It is the only overdamped house spring, so it never passes the end value.

springs.name: vawe playful
springs.note: It is the house spring that overshoots most.

springs.name: react-spring default
springs.conversion: Stiffness is tension and damping is friction, with mass 1 (the default). The physics loop in the same package, acceleration = (-tension x displacement - friction x velocity) / mass, is the spring that spring() in springs.js solves.
springs.note: It is the config a spring gets when you pass none. The numbers equal vawe default.

springs.name: react-spring gentle
springs.conversion: Stiffness is tension and damping is friction, with mass 1 (the default). The physics loop in the same package, acceleration = (-tension x displacement - friction x velocity) / mass, is the spring that spring() in springs.js solves.
springs.note: Its stiffness is lower than default (120 against 170) and its damping is about half (14 against 26).

springs.name: react-spring wobbly
springs.conversion: Stiffness is tension and damping is friction, with mass 1 (the default). The physics loop in the same package, acceleration = (-tension x displacement - friction x velocity) / mass, is the spring that spring() in springs.js solves.
springs.note: Of the six react-spring presets it overshoots the most.

springs.name: react-spring stiff
springs.conversion: Stiffness is tension and damping is friction, with mass 1 (the default). The physics loop in the same package, acceleration = (-tension x displacement - friction x velocity) / mass, is the spring that spring() in springs.js solves.
springs.note: Its settle time is about the same as default (0.715 s against 0.705 s), but default does not overshoot.

springs.name: react-spring slow
springs.conversion: Stiffness is tension and damping is friction, with mass 1 (the default). The physics loop in the same package, acceleration = (-tension x displacement - friction x velocity) / mass, is the spring that spring() in springs.js solves.
springs.note: Its tension (280) is the same as molasses; only the friction differs (60 against 120).

springs.name: react-spring molasses
springs.conversion: Stiffness is tension and damping is friction, with mass 1 (the default). The physics loop in the same package, acceleration = (-tension x displacement - friction x velocity) / mass, is the spring that spring() in springs.js solves.
springs.note: It is the slowest preset in this set, 2.915 s. Its damping ratio is 3.59, so the extra friction holds the spring back.

springs.name: Motion default spring
springs.original: transition: { type: "spring" } with no other option: stiffness 100, damping 10, mass 1
springs.conversion: Stiffness and damping are used as they are, with mass 1.
springs.note: Motion uses it for a spring you declare with type "spring" and no other numbers.

springs.name: Motion x, y and rotate default
springs.conversion: Stiffness and damping are used as they are, with mass 1.
springs.note: Motion uses it for a transform value (x, y, rotate) with two keyframes, when you set no transition. A scale value gets the next preset.

springs.name: Motion scale default
springs.original: criticallyDampedSpring(target) = { type: "spring", stiffness: 550, damping: target === 0 ? 2 * Math.sqrt(550) : 30, restSpeed: 10 }
springs.conversion: Stiffness and damping are used as they are, with mass 1.
springs.note: The source calls it criticallyDampedSpring, but damping 30 is below critical for stiffness 550, which is 2 x sqrt(550), about 46.9. Motion uses that value only when a scale animates to 0.

springs.name: SwiftUI spring()
springs.conversion: stiffness = (2 pi / response)^2, damping = 4 pi x dampingFraction / response, with mass 1. The duration-and-bounce forms map to response = duration and dampingFraction = 1 - bounce, the same bounce mapping Motion documents "as SwiftUI does". Apple states bounce 0 is critically damped and bounce 1 is undamped.
springs.note: A damping fraction of 0.825 is the documented default of spring(response:dampingFraction:blendDuration:).

springs.name: SwiftUI .smooth
springs.conversion: stiffness = (2 pi / response)^2, damping = 4 pi x dampingFraction / response, with mass 1. The duration-and-bounce forms map to response = duration and dampingFraction = 1 - bounce, the same bounce mapping Motion documents "as SwiftUI does". Apple states bounce 0 is critically damped and bounce 1 is undamped.
springs.note: Bounce 0 means a critically damped spring: the fastest settle with no overshoot.

springs.name: SwiftUI .snappy
springs.original: .snappy: duration 0.5, base bounce 0.15 (Apple: "small amount of bounce")
springs.conversion: stiffness = (2 pi / response)^2, damping = 4 pi x dampingFraction / response, with mass 1. The duration-and-bounce forms map to response = duration and dampingFraction = 1 - bounce, the same bounce mapping Motion documents "as SwiftUI does". Apple states bounce 0 is critically damped and bounce 1 is undamped.
springs.note: Its base bounce of 0.15 gives a damping fraction of 0.85.

springs.name: SwiftUI .bouncy
springs.original: .bouncy: duration 0.5, base bounce 0.3 (Apple: "higher amount of bounce")
springs.conversion: stiffness = (2 pi / response)^2, damping = 4 pi x dampingFraction / response, with mass 1. The duration-and-bounce forms map to response = duration and dampingFraction = 1 - bounce, the same bounce mapping Motion documents "as SwiftUI does". Apple states bounce 0 is critically damped and bounce 1 is undamped.
springs.note: Its base bounce of 0.3 gives a damping fraction of 0.7.

springs.name: Compose spring() default

source.file: spring() in AnimationSpec.kt: dampingRatio = DampingRatioNoBouncy (1), stiffness = StiffnessMedium (1500)

springs.conversion: Stiffness is used as it is with mass 1 (SpringSimulation takes the natural frequency as sqrt(stiffness)). damping = 2 x dampingRatio x sqrt(stiffness), the same c = 2 x naturalFreq x dampingRatio that SpringSimulation.getAcceleration uses.
springs.note: Stiffness 1500 with critical damping gives the shortest settle in this set, 0.24 s.

springs.note: DampingRatioHighBouncy, 0.2, is the lowest damping ratio constant in the Spring object.

springs.name: Material 3 Expressive default spatial

springs.note: Material 3 documents the default spatial spec for animations that may change the shape or bounds of a component.

springs.name: Material 3 Expressive slow spatial
springs.conversion: Stiffness is used as it is with mass 1 (SpringSimulation takes the natural frequency as sqrt(stiffness)). damping = 2 x dampingRatio x sqrt(stiffness), the same c = 2 x naturalFreq x dampingRatio that SpringSimulation.getAcceleration uses.
springs.note: It has the same damping ratio as the default spatial spring (0.8). Only the stiffness is lower, 200 against 380.

springs.name: Material 3 Standard default spatial
springs.conversion: Stiffness is used as it is with mass 1 (SpringSimulation takes the natural frequency as sqrt(stiffness)). damping = 2 x dampingRatio x sqrt(stiffness), the same c = 2 x naturalFreq x dampingRatio that SpringSimulation.getAcceleration uses.
springs.note: Its damping ratio is 0.9, against 0.8 and 0.6 in the Expressive scheme.
